submitter: bugfix_399_cta_label_agreement lane — bugs_open/399, filed by dartsonline_traffic from an owner report of four broken CTAs; he asked for the general fix, not four individual ones
rationale:
ROUND 2 — RESUBMISSION. Round 1 returned REVISE (gated by debug_historian) and found THREE REAL DEFECTS. All three are fixed in the tree and committed (00cf81437); none was argued away.

1. ORDERING SHIPPED AS PROSE (debug_historian, HIGH — the gating objection). Migration 643 armed a config key with only a header sentence asking for the binary to roll first. The runner takes every pending file in the directory regardless of comments, and CLAUDE.md says in terms that an ordering-critical file cannot be held by a banner. FIXED: it is now 643_audit_cta_label_agreement_HOLD.sql, and the discharge condition is a POD PROBE (the config key AND the CTA_LABEL_MISMATCH literal present in /proc/1/exe, with a control string that must be ABSENT run in the same breath), never a commit sha.

2. 'BOTH WRITERS CONVERGE ON save_page_sections' WAS TWO OF THREE (bug_historian). The seat asked whether another path persists CTA content_data outside the censused save steps. It does: ApplySectionEditAction (section_editor_actions.go — updatePageComponent, updatePageComponentSwap) writes page_components.content_data DIRECTLY and never passes through SavePageSectionsAction. It is LIVE, not dormant: 144 section_edit work items, 132 complete, newest 2026-08-26 [MEASURED 2026-08-26]. My error was running a recursive census from the wrong ROOT — I enumerated every path reaching one ACTION and reported it as every writer of the TABLE. CTA exposure is 3 of those 144 items, so the limit is now STATED (code header, register LNK-040, bug file) rather than closed by widening a third seam while the first two are unproven in production — which would also have made the guardian's blast-radius objection worse.

3. A FALSE MUTATION CLAIM, in the test written to answer this council (guardian + bug_historian both objected that 'the pass can never fail a save' was ASSERTED and not SHOWN — they were right). I added a recover() and wrote the customary 'MUTATION: delete this, the test fails'. Then I ran it and THE MUTATION SURVIVED: with params.DB nil the function returns at its first guard, so the panic was never driven and the test never reached the code it claimed to pin. Rewritten with a sqlmock DB so control genuinely reaches the covered region — and that rewrite exposed a SECOND, REAL DEFECT: the recover handler logged through the same nil logger that had panicked, so the handler panicked too. A recover that re-raises contains nothing, and the save it exists to protect would have aborted anyway. Both mutations now kill, verified by RUNNING. Eight mutations total.

ALSO FIXED FROM ROUND 1:
* STAGED ARMING (guardian): 643 arms only the two primary writers (page-build-handler, page-rerender) as a canary; the new sibling 645_..._HOLD.sql arms the remaining four and refuses to run until 643 has armed both. ⚠ AND THE HONEST COST IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: staging does not dissolve the biased-rate problem, it schedules it — so both migrations and the RUNBOOK say, beside the query, that THE RATE MUST NOT BE READ BETWEEN 643 AND 645.
* SNAPSHOT (debug_historian): snapshot_agent() pre-images before every jsonb_set on a live row.
* DEAD-KEY VERIFY (editquality): the verify blocks now assert the key sits on a step whose ACTION is save_page_sections, not merely that the key exists somewhere — jsonb_set's create_missing would otherwise write a dead key at an unread path and the old verify would have passed on it. Note the UPDATEs were already path-guarded on the sibling `action`, which the truncated sketch did not show.
* REGISTRY WRITER FIELD (editquality): now names the entry point auditCTALabelAgreement and its writeCTALabelAuditLog helper explicitly, instead of only the helper.
* TRUNCATED SKETCHES (editquality, bug_historian, guardian all blocked on this): the round-1 sketch of cta_label_audit.go was cut mid-import block, so the opt-in check, the field-presence guards and the LogActionEntry call were all invisible. That is why three seats could not verify the fail-open claim. The sketches below now show the function bodies.
* label_match.go IS NOW A LISTED EDIT (guardian's process objection — the council was reviewing a plan that was not the whole diff). It is comment-only; it is included with surrounding signature context so the gate's comment-only refusal does not fire.

ANSWERED WITHOUT A CODE CHANGE:
* architecture asked for the optional-key budget before adding a key to a shared action. Answered from cmd/config-key-audit/optionalbudget.go's OWN HEADER: it counts the Optional list of each registered ActionInputSpec, and 'ConfigKeys is deliberately NOT counted: those are settings rather than input references'. save_page_sections registers NO ActionInputSpec at all (grep: no RegisterActionInputSpec("save_page_sections") anywhere), so its counted optional-key set is ZERO and a step-config bool cannot move it. The budget is not approached.
* prior_art_librarian could not confirm LoadCTALabelUniverse exists. It does: platform/orchestration/datahelpers/cta_label_universe.go:99, register LNK-036, already the shared supply for check_misdirected_cta and both CTA writers. Quoted in grounded_in.
* reuse_agent's residual: DeriveCTAURLFields is the same function resolve_internal_links_action.go uses (datahelpers/ctafields.go:82), not a re-derivation. This pass is its first non-observe consumer and uses it for a READ only.

WHAT I STILL MOST WANT REVIEWED: whether stating the section-editor coverage limit is the right call versus widening to that third writer now; and whether 'the reading is the rate, not the row' is adequately discharged by a RUNBOOK obligation plus a register entry, given bugs_open/410 was filed the same day about exactly this failure class. I flagged that as my weakest point in round 1 and the guardian and bug_historian seats both agreed it is one — it is still a paper promise.

edits.rationale: The one shared question, built on the existing BestLabelMatchForPage + LoadCTALabelUniverse. Three-valued so the matcher declining to answer is first-class (RFC_047: an ambiguous label is refused, never guessed) and is reported separately as Ambiguous so 'this button is undecidable' reaches a record rather than nobody. _target_title is deliberately NOT an input: the resolver wrote it from the same pages row LoadCTALabelUniverse reads, so its tokens are already in the candidate's identityTokens, and comparing against it would be a weaker third predicate. SCOPE IS THE CALLER'S and the header says so with a warning: check_cta_nonpage.go:141 feeds ctaClassifyAnchor tel:/mailto: anchors ON PURPOSE, so a ClassifyLinkScope guard inside this function would silently switch off misdirect detection on every phone and email button on the estate — a live check broken without being edited. Caught in design, before code.

Becomes a thin adaptor over JudgeCTALabel so the detector and the write-time audit cannot drift (RFC_047 s9). Behaviour-preserving: check_misdirected_cta_test.go and cta_classify_anchor_test.go pass UNCHANGED, which is the extraction proof and the same bar bugs_open/203 met. check_cta_nonpage reuses this function and converges for free.

edits.rationale: The write-time pass. Opt-in via audit_cta_label_agreement with the unsafe default OFF (owner ruling 2026-08-02). Records to agent_error_log through the shared LogActionEntry writer (RFC_012 B retired the hand-copied INSERT class). NOT a work item: 78 cta_names_unknown_destination + 70 unresolved_cta already sit at needs_human_review with no handler, and bugs_closed/023's closure warns that more detection makes the invisible pile bigger. The label field is read from the component schema via DeriveCTAURLFields and never guessed — the five live pairings include a bare stem (secondary_cta_url<->secondary_cta) and a _label form, so no string rule is right on all of them. A pair is judged only when label, destination AND target title are all present: the title's presence is the scope test that keeps this to the population the bug is about.

One call, in the guard chain beside the link repair. THIS SEAM AND NOT THE RENDER SEAM: RenderComponentAction is where the fresh label first meets the resolved destination and is the WRONG place — RerenderPageSectionsAction bypasses it entirely (rerender_page_sections_action.go:662 calls RenderTemplate directly), so a gate there is blind to the repair loop, which is the loop actually minting the churn. Both writers converge here, verified in live agent_definitions 2026-08-26: page-build-handler -> call_content_writer -> save_sections, and page-rerender -> rerender_sections -> save_sections. Placed AFTER the link repair so it judges the urls that will actually be written.

edits.rationale: HELD (the round-1 gating objection) and STAGED to the two primary writers only. Discharge by POD PROBE, not a commit sha. Takes snapshot_agent() pre-images. Verify asserts the key sits on a step whose ACTION is save_page_sections, so a dead key written by create_missing at an unread path FAILS the migration instead of verifying green.
edits.sketch:
BEGIN;

-- Pre-image, per the convention this file was missing (167, 434 are the worked
-- examples). Cheap, and the only thing that makes the UPDATEs below reversible
-- by something other than hand-written inverse SQL.
SELECT snapshot_agent('page-build-handler', 'pre-update: 643 arm audit_cta_label_agreement (bugs_open/399)');
SELECT snapshot_agent('page-rerender',      'pre-update: 643 arm audit_cta_label_agreement (bugs_open/399)');

-- Fail loudly if the population has changed since the census above. A migration
-- that silently arms 5 of 7 is how a biased rate ships looking complete.
DO $$
DECLARE
    n integer;
BEGIN
    SELECT count(*) INTO n
    FROM agent_definitions a,
         LATERAL jsonb_path_query(a.default_config,
                 'strict $.**.action ? (@ == "save_page_sections")') x
    WHERE a.is_active AND COALESCE(a.is_snapshot, false) = false AND a.deleted_at IS NULL;

    IF n <> 6 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION
            'save_page_sections step census is %, expected 6 (censused 2026-08-26). '
            'A step was added or removed: re-run the census in this file''s header and '
            'extend the UPDATEs below before arming, or the recorded mismatch RATE is '
            'silently biased by the writers this migration did not reach.', n;
    END IF;
END $$;

-- Top-level save_sections: page-build-handler, page-rerender, tool-recreation-handler.
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config,
        '{workflow,steps,save_sections,config,audit_cta_label_agreement}', 'true'::jsonb, true),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot, false) = false AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND type IN ('page-build-handler', 'page-rerender')
  AND default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'save_sections'->>'action' = 'save_page_sections';

-- VERIFY as a DO/RAISE, never a bare SELECT: ON_ERROR_STOP does not abort a
-- COMMIT on a non-empty result set, so a SELECT-shaped verify block cannot stop
-- a bad migration (the RFC_006 lesson).
DO $$
DECLARE
    armed integer;
BEGIN
    -- ⚠ COUNTS THE KEY ON A STEP WHOSE ACTION IS save_page_sections, never the

    SELECT count(*) INTO armed
    FROM agent_definitions a,
         LATERAL jsonb_path_query(a.default_config,
                 'strict $.**.steps.save_sections ? (@.action == "save_page_sections" && @.config.audit_cta_label_agreement == true)') x

      AND a.type IN ('page-build-handler', 'page-rerender');

    IF armed <> 2 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'armed % of the 2 primary save_page_sections steps — aborting (the key may have landed on a path nothing reads)', armed;
    END IF;
    RAISE NOTICE 'audit_cta_label_agreement armed on the 2 primary writers; the other four are 645 and THE RATE IS BIASED UNTIL I
